text.title: Architect Skill Index (Geek Tier) Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules every curated architect skill index MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Every index entry MUST point at an existing methodology directory under `skills/faion/knowledge/` by wikilink slug, and the target's `meta.json` MUST have `status: active`. Entries whose slug does not resolve, or whose target is `draft`, are rejected at review. The index authors no methodology bodies of its own.

rationale.source: Faion knowledge-base linking convention (wikilinks resolve to a methodology directory; meta.json status field)

rule.rationale: The whole value of the index is that it closes a perceived coverage gap without writing new content. One dangling link teaches the architect that the index is decorative, and a link to a draft hands them a document that will change under them.

rule.statement: Each entry MUST carry a one-sentence architect-perspective "why" that names the architecture task the entry serves (boundary decision, ADR, fitness function, quality-attribute trade-off, review of a cross-cutting change). The sentence MUST NOT be the target's own one-sentence summary or a paraphrase of it; a reviewer diffs the two.

rationale.source: Ford, Parsons and Kua, 'Building Evolutionary Architectures'; Bass, Clements and Kazman, 'Software Architecture in Practice'

rule.rationale: The sdlc-ai entries were written for developers: spec-kit as "write the spec first", plan-mode as "plan before coding". Re-anchoring is the only thing this index adds; copying the summary yields a table of contents the architect could have grepped.

rule.statement: Entries MUST be grouped into named clusters that correspond to architecture activities (for example: eliciting architecturally significant requirements, deciding and recording, documenting views, evaluating and reviewing, governing drift), never by the source tool or feature name (spec-kit, plan-mode, RAG). Every cluster has at least three entries or is merged.

rationale.source: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 (architecture description: stakeholders, concerns, viewpoints); SEI architecture practice (Bass, Clements, Kazman)

rule.rationale: An architect arrives with a task ("I have to review a boundary change"), not with a tool name. Tool-named clusters force them to already know which tool maps to the task, which is precisely the knowledge the index was supposed to supply.

rule.statement: The index MUST contain at least 50 entries, and each target slug MUST appear exactly once. A count below 50 is reported as a gap (see `r-uncovered-tasks-listed`), never padded with near-duplicates, and a slug listed under two clusters is a defect.

rationale.source: Faion geek-tier index definition (50+ entries); widely established practice in curated indexes

rule.rationale: The 50 figure is the promise the tier makes. Meeting it by listing the same methodology under three clusters, or by adding entries with no architectural angle, produces a longer index that is harder to scan and still misses the tasks the architect came for.

rule.statement: Every entry MUST have exactly these fields: `slug` (wikilink), `cluster`, `architect_why` (one sentence), `load_when` (the observable trigger that says to open it), and `est_tokens` (copied from the target's `meta.json`). Free-form entries and entries missing `load_when` are rejected.

rationale.source: Faion meta.json schema (est_tokens, tier, status); progressive-disclosure practice in agent skill design

rule.rationale: The index is read by an agent as often as by a person, and the agent decides whether to load a 2,400-token document from the entry alone. Without `load_when` and `est_tokens` it either loads everything or nothing; both waste the context budget the index exists to protect.

rule.statement: The index MUST end with an explicit "not covered" section listing architecture tasks for which no active methodology exists, each as one line naming the task and the closest partial match (or "none"). An index with no such section is treated as unreviewed.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in curated documentation (scope statements and known-gaps sections)

rule.rationale: The coverage gap this index closes is "perceived". The honest way to close it is to show what is actually covered and what is not; an index that implies completeness sends the architect searching for an entry that does not exist, and they conclude the whole tier is unreliable.

rule.statement: At each review cadence every wikilink MUST be re-resolved and every `est_tokens` re-read from the target's `meta.json`; entries whose target has moved, been deprecated or is no longer `active` are removed or re-pointed in the same review, and the review run's output is linked in `evidence[]`.

rationale.source: Faion meta.json lifecycle (status, last_reviewed); link-rot practice in documentation maintenance

rule.rationale: Methodologies are renamed and merged as the corpus grows. An index is the artefact most exposed to that churn because it does nothing but point elsewhere; a scripted relink at cadence is the cheapest way to keep it from rotting silently.
